subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Discount and Marked Price — Successive Discounts, Profit + Discount (W11 B1)

questions.stem: A book is marked at ₹500 and sold at a discount of 20%. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: C is correct. SP = MP × (1 − discount%/100) = 500 × (1 − 20/100) = 500 × 0.8 = ₹400. Trap: ₹350 = 500 × 0.7 (30% discount); ₹420 = 500 × 0.84 (16% discount); ₹380 = wrong computation.

questions.stem: An item is marked at ₹800 and sold for ₹680. What is the discount percentage?
A shopkeeper marks his goods 25% above cost price and then gives a discount of 10%. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Let CP = 100. MP = 125. SP = 125×0.9 = 112.5. Profit% = (112.5−100)/100 × 100 = 12.5%. Shortcut: profit% = (1+m/100)(1−d/100)−1 = 1.25×0.9−1 = 1.125−1 = 12.5%. Trap: 15% = MP%−discount% (wrong subtraction); 10% = just the discount (ignores markup).

questions.stem: A product with a marked price of ₹1,000 is sold after two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the final selling price?
questions.explanation: B is correct. After first 20% discount: 1000×0.8 = ₹800. After second 10% discount: 800×0.9 = ₹720. Net equivalent single discount = 20+10−(20×10)/100 = 28%. SP = 1000×0.72 = ₹720 ✓. Trap: ₹700 = 1000×(1−30%) (adds discounts simply: 20+10=30); ₹750 = 1000×0.75 (25% discount — midpoint).

questions.stem: A trader marks goods 40% above cost price and offers a 25% discount. Find the profit or loss percentage.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Let CP = 100. MP = 140. SP = 140×0.75 = 105. Profit% = 5%. Shortcut: profit% = (1+40/100)(1−25/100)−1 = 1.40×0.75−1 = 1.05−1 = 0.05 = 5%. Trap: 0% = thinking 40% markup and 25% discount cancel (they don't — markups and discounts have different bases); 10% = adding 40−25−5 wrong.

questions.stem: What single discount is equivalent to two successive discounts of 30% and 20%?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Equivalent single discount = x+y−xy/100 = 30+20−(30×20)/100 = 50−6 = 44%. Verify: MP = 100. After 30%: SP₁ = 70. After 20%: SP₂ = 70×0.8 = 56. Single discount = 100−56 = 44% ✓. Trap: 50% = simple sum of 30+20; 42% = 30+20−8 (wrong product term); 46% = 30+20−4 (wrong).

questions.stem: An article with a marked price of ₹1,200 is sold after two equal successive discounts. If the final selling price is ₹768, what is the rate of each discount?
A shopkeeper earns a profit of 12% after selling an article at a 20% discount on the marked price. What is the ratio of the cost price to the marked price?
questions.explanation: B is correct. SP = MP×0.8 and SP = CP×1.12. So CP×1.12 = MP×0.8 → CP/MP = 0.8/1.12 = 80/112 = 5/7. CP:MP = 5:7. Trap: 4:5 = 0.8/1 (ignores profit factor); 7:10 = wrong ratio; 3:4 = another incorrect ratio.

questions.stem: A television is sold at a profit of 15% after giving a discount of 8% on the marked price. By what percentage is the marked price above the cost price?
questions.explanation: C is correct. SP = MP×0.92 = CP×1.15. MP = CP×(1.15/0.92) = CP×1.25. So MP is 25% above CP. Verify: if CP=100, MP=125, SP=125×0.92=115=CP×1.15 ✓. Trap: 23% = 15+8 (adds the rates); 20% = some wrong computation; 27% = another wrong combination.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold at the same selling price of ₹600 each. One is sold at a profit of 20% and the other at a loss of 20%. What is the overall result?
questions.explanation: C is correct. CP₁ = 600/1.20 = ₹500. CP₂ = 600/0.80 = ₹750. Total CP = 1250. Total SP = 1200. Loss = 50. Loss% = 50/1250 × 100 = 4%. Formula: when the same SP is charged, one at x% profit and one at x% loss, overall loss% = x²/100 = 20²/100 = 4%. Trap: 0% = assumes gains and losses cancel equally (they don't because CPs are different); Gain of 4% = wrong sign.
